title: Network Retrieval Command Piped Directly To A Shell
detection_hypothesis: If remote code is executed without staging, the command line will contain a retrieval utility and a pipe into a shell in the same invocation.

field_semantics.CommandLine: Full command line including arguments as supplied to the process.

collection_prerequisites: An execve audit rule or equivalent process telemetry agent is deployed.
Audit rules are not limited to a narrow allowlist of binaries.
expected_collection_gaps: Containers without a shared audit namespace may not report execve records.
Audit backlog limits can drop records under load.
normalization_assumptions: Image is the absolute executable path and CommandLine is the joined argument vector.
ParentImage identifies the parent executable path.
ingestion_differences: auditd argument vectors may be hex-encoded before normalization.
Some agents report the argv array instead of a joined string.
retention_considerations: Execve telemetry is high volume; 30 to 60 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Low on production servers; higher on build agents.
false_positive_strategy: Benign matches point at internal artefact hosts and occur on build or developer systems. Tune on the destination host inside the command line together with the host role.
tuning_guidance: Exclude the internal artefact hostname on build agents. Do not exclude the pipe pattern, which is the behavioural core of the rule.
test_strategy: Positive cases use two different retrieval utilities. Negative cases retrieve to a file, pipe a local file into a shell, and reference the pattern inside a documentation command.

attack_techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell

author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
